title: Acrocorinth
visualBrief: Fortified twin ridge with three successive western gates,surviving terrain-following curtains,inner towers,rectangular Ottoman summit keep,citadel,cistern terrace and selected roofless remains. A relative terrain study,not a flat site-boundary extrusion.

identityFeatures: Twin rocky ridge with surviving terrain-following curtains

Small rectangular southwest Ottoman keep within its own citadel

The runtime derivative omits the embedded research terrain mesh and samples its architectural footing functions directly from standard viewer PMTiles, using a0.7m working clearance. The old relative258.37m datum remains only in the preserved source master. The broad site ring is contextual; footprint replacement stays off. Anchor 22.873283683,37.891346465; heading -0.026117351143; standard PMTiles datum 510.43219632278726m. Floors are reconstructed and foundations extend below the coarse sampled ground.

limitations: Approximate current surviving exterior from inspected picture and standard viewer PMTiles; no bespoke survey or exact thresholds.
Original detailed master and adapted ASCSA wall data preserved with their CC-BY-SA attribution. Independent derivative uses viewer terrain for footing and omits embedded hill mesh.
Twin ridge curtains, successive gates, inner towers, Ottoman keep/citadel, cistern terrace and selected roofless remains retain identity. Architectural heights and thresholds reconstructed.
Site boundary is context, not a wall footprint; replacement remains off. Selected surviving walls and remains do not imply archaeological completeness.
Host provides ridge terrain. Modern roads, vegetation, fixtures, interiors, buried remains and lost roofs excluded.
Two common material graphs and local recess color; no embedded images. Physical-device timing pending.
importReason: Preserve Acrocorinth ridge,successive gate hierarchy and open ruins with shared materials and independent compact detail levels.
